verses.zh: 十二年十二月初一日，耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: In the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, on the first of the month,[NOTE:1] the Lord’s message came to me:
notes: This would be March 3, 585 b.c.
verses.commentary: 32:1 See note at Ezek. 29:1. This date would be about one year after the fall of Jerusalem in 586 B.C.

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要为埃及王法老作哀歌，说：从前你在列国中，如同少壮狮子；现在你却像海中的大鱼。你冲出江河，用爪搅动诸水，使江河浑浊。
verses.en: “Son of man, sing a lament for Pharaoh king of Egypt, and say to him:“‘You were like a lion[NOTE:1] among the nations,but you are a monster in the seas;you thrash about in your streams,stir up the water with your feet,and muddy your[NOTE:2] streams.
notes: The lion was a figure of royalty (Ezek 19:1-9).
The Hebrew reads, “their streams”; the LXX reads, “your streams.”
verses.commentary:
32:2 The four-chapter litany of judgment against Egypt continues (i.e. chapters 29-32).

▣ "take up a lamentation" A lamentation denoted a well known form of poetic meter ( BDB 884, cf.
Ezek. 2:10; 19:1,14 [twice]; 26:17; 27:2,32; 28:12; 32:16; Jer. 9:10,20). This chapter, like 19:1; 27:2;
28:12, starts with a command for a funeral dirge ("take up," BDB 669, KB 724, Qal
IMPERATIVE, cf. Jer. 7:29). Isaiah 14:4 has the same VERB
in Qal PERFECT, but with "taunt" or "proverb" (BDB 605).

▣ "You compared yourself to a young lion of the nations" Again this is a reference to Pharaoh's
pride and arrogance (cf. Ezek. 29:3; 30:6; 31:2-9,10; 32:12). He was not a lion, but a water creature.

Special Topic: Lions in the OT

NASB, NKJV, REB, Peshitta
"like the monster"

NRSV, JPSOA
"like a dragon"

TEV, NJB
"like a crocodile"

LXX
"like a serpent"

See full note at Ezek. 29:3. This may be an allusion to Canaanite mythology where Ba'al
defeats Yam, or Babylonian mythology where Marduk defeats Tiamat. The OT alluded to
these myths without acknowledging their reality (e.g. Isa. 27:1).

The UBS Text Project, p. 105, gives "crocodile" an "A" rating

Special Topic: The Serpent

Special Topic: Leviathan

Special Topic: The Great Red Dragon

Special Topic: ANE Creation and Flood Myths

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：我必用多国的人民，将我的网撒在你身上，把你拉上来。
verses.en: “‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says:“‘I will throw my net over you[NOTE:1] in the assembly of many peoples;and they will haul you up in my dragnet.
notes: The expression “throw my net” is common in Ezekiel (12:13; 17:20; 19:8).
verses.commentary:
32:3-7 The language of ANE cursing is dramatic hyperbole. It is difficult for literalistic westerners to understand this genre.
A good brief chapter, "How does the language of destruction and blessing work?" in D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks:
Rethinking the Language of Biblical Prophecy and Apocalyptic, pp. 75-102, has been helpful to me. I hope you will read it.

Two other books in this same area of a genre-related approach to biblical interpretation arre

- G. B. Caird, The Language and Imagery of the Bible

- Gordon Fee and Douglas Stuart, How To Read the Bible For All Its Worth

32:3 In Ezek. 29:4 YHWH uses a hook, here a net (cf. Ezek. 12:13; 17:20). This is also described in mythological terms in Ps. 74:13-14.
For the different types of mythology, see book #1 above, pp.219-242.

verses.zh: 我必将你丢在地上，抛在田野，使空中的飞鸟都落在你身上，使遍地的野兽吃你得饱。
verses.en: I will leave you on the ground,I will fling you on the open field,I will allow[NOTE:1] all the birds of the sky to settle[NOTE:2] on you,and I will permit[NOTE:3] all the wild animals[NOTE:4] to gorge themselves on you.
notes: Or “cause.”
Heb “live.”
Or “cause.”
Heb “the beasts of the field,” referring to wild as opposed to domesticated animals.
verses.commentary: 32:4 This same ignominious fate (i.e. unburied and eaten by animals) is described in Ezek. 29:5; 39:4. It reflects the curse of Deut. 28:26.

verses.zh: 我必将你的肉丢在山间，用你高大的尸首填满山谷。
verses.en: I will put your flesh on the mountains,and fill the valleys with your maggot-infested carcass.[NOTE:1]
notes: The Hebrew text is difficult here, apparently meaning “your height.” Following Symmachus and the Syriac, it is preferable to emend the text to read “your maggots.” See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:203.
verses.commentary:
32:5

NASB
"refuse"

NKJV
"carcass"

Peshitta
"dust"

TEV, JPSOA
"rotting corpse"

NJB
"corruption"

REB
"worms that fed on it"

The REB assumes that the MT's "with your height," רמות (BDB 928, KB 1242)
should be רממ (BDB 942, KB 1244 I, "be wormy," cf. Exod. 16:20). Some see a parallel
to Isa. 14:11 to "maggots" רמה (BDB 942, KB 1241, see NET Bible).

verses.zh: 我又必用你的血浇灌你所游泳之地，漫过山顶；河道都必充满。
verses.en: I will drench the land with the flow of your blood up to the mountains, and the ravines will be full of your blood.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “from you.”
verses.commentary:
32:6

NASB, NKJV, NRSV
"flowing blood"

LXX
"dung"

NEB
"discharge"

JPSOA
"oozing blood"

TEV, NJB, REB, Peshitta
"blood"

The MT has two NOUNS.

- with your out flow ‒ BDB 847 (see NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 833)

- blood ‒ BDB 196

The first NOUN is found only here in all the OT.

Special Topic: Blood

verses.zh: 我将你扑灭的时候，要把天遮蔽，使众星昏暗，以密云遮掩太阳，月亮也不放光。
verses.en: When I extinguish you, I will cover the sky;I will darken its stars.I will cover the sun with a cloud,and the moon will not shine.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “will not shine its light.” For similar features of cosmic eschatology, see Joel 2:10; 3:15; Amos 5:18-20; Zeph 1:5.
verses.commentary:
32:7-8 As the Genesis creation account (Genesis 1) depreciates the astral deities of Babylon, these
verses depreciate the astral deities of Egypt. The darkness shows YHWH's power over Ra, the sun god.

- "make dark," BDB 871, KB 1072 (Hiphil found only in Ezekiel, 3 times, cf. Ezek. 31:15)

- Hiphil PERFECT with waw, Ezek. 32:7

- Hiphil IMPERFECT, Ezek. 32:8

- "darkness," BDB 365 (cf. Gen. 1:2; Exod. 10:22; Amos 5:18,20)

Special Topic: Darkness, I.

verses.zh: 我必使天上的亮光都在你以上变为昏暗，使你的地上黑暗。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: I will darken all the lights in the sky over you,and I will darken your land,declares the Sovereign Lord.

verses.zh: 「我使你败亡的风声传到你所不认识的各国。那时，我必使多民的心因你愁烦。
verses.en: I will disturb[NOTE:1] many peopleswhen I bring about your destruction among the nations,among countries you do not know.
notes: Heb “I will provoke the heart of.”
verses.commentary:
32:9-10 This is a common theme in these chapters (cf. Ezek. 32:16,19; 27:29-36; 28:19). YHWH's judgment on
prideful Tyre and Egypt was meant to send a message to the nations (i.e. they will know that I am the Lord,
e.g. Ezek. 32:15; 29:9; 33:29; 35:3,4,9,14).

32:9

NASB, NKJV, TEB, NJB, NET
"bring your destruction"

NRSV, LXX
"carry you captive"

REB
"bring your broken army"

JPSOA
"bring your shattered

remnants"

Peshitta
"bring the news of your

destruction"

The UBS Text Project, p. 106, gives the MT's "destruction" a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

- MT ‒ שׁבר, BDB 991 I, #4, KB 1402-1406 (i.e. break, fracture, crush)

- LXX ‒ שׁבי, BDB 985, #3 (i.e. captives)

verses.zh: 我在许多国民和君王面前向你抡我的刀，国民就必因你惊奇，君王也必因你极其恐慌。在你仆倒的日子，他们各人为自己的性命时刻战兢。」
verses.en: I will shock many peoples with you,and their kings will shiver with horror because of you.When I brandish my sword before them,every moment each one will tremble for his life, on the day of your fall.
verses.commentary:
32:10 "shall be horribly afraid" This is the NOUN and VERB (Qal IMPERFECT)
of the same root (BDB 972, KB 1343, cf. Ezek. 27:35; Jer. 2:12), which denotes the hair standing up in fear.

▣ "they shall tremble" This term (BDB 353, KB 350, Qal PERFECT
with waw) denotes fear in YHWH"s coming and present judgment (cf. Ezek. 26:16,18; 30:9; note Heb. 10:31).

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：「巴比伦王的刀必临到你。
verses.en: “‘For this is what the Sovereign Lord says: “‘The sword of the king of Babylon[NOTE:1] will attack[NOTE:2] you.
notes: The king of Babylon referred to here was Nebuchadnezzar (Ezek 21:19).
Heb “approach.”
verses.commentary:
32:11 Nebuchadnezzar II was YHWH's instrument of judgment (cf. Ezek. 21:19), as Assyria had been
(cf. Isa. 10:5) and Cyrus II will be (cf. Isa. 44:28; 45:7).

verses.zh: 我必藉勇士的刀使你的众民仆倒；这勇士都是列国中强暴的。他们必使埃及的骄傲归于无有；埃及的众民必被灭绝。
verses.en: By the swords of the mighty warriors I will cause your hordes to fall—all of them are the most terrifying among the nations.They will devastate the pride of Egypt,and all its hordes will be destroyed.

verses.zh: 我必从埃及多水旁除灭所有的走兽；人脚兽蹄必不再搅浑这水。
verses.en: I will destroy all its cattle beside the plentiful waters;and no human foot will disturb[NOTE:1] the waters[NOTE:2] again,nor will the hooves of cattle disturb them.
notes: Heb “muddy.”
Heb “them,” that is, the waters mentioned in the previous line. The translation clarifies the referent.
verses.commentary: 32:13 This could be another way of depreciating the gods of Egypt, as did the ten plagues in the Exodus.

verses.zh: 那时，我必使埃及河澄清，江河像油缓流。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: Then I will make their waters calm[NOTE:1] and will make their streams flow like olive oil, declares the Sovereign Lord.
notes: Heb “sink,” that is, to settle and become clear, not muddied.
verses.commentary:
32:14 The waters of Egypt will be undisturbed (clear and settled) by any animal or human. No one will be
left alive. This imagery for total destruction is found only here.

verses.zh: 我使埃及地变为荒废凄凉；这地缺少从前所充满的，又击杀其中一切的居民。那时，他们就知道我是耶和华。
verses.en: When I turn the land of Egypt into desolation and the land is destitute of everything that fills it,when I strike all those who live in it,then they will know that I am the Lord.’

verses.zh: 「人必用这哀歌去哀哭，列国的女子为埃及和她的群众也必以此悲哀。这是主耶和华说的。」
verses.en: This is a lament; they will chant it.The daughters of the nations will chant it.They will chant it over Egypt and over all her hordes,declares the Sovereign Lord.”
verses.commentary:
32:16 The professional wailers and mourners (BDB 884, 1096 three times) would be from all the nations.

- those who were helped and protected by Egypt (Ezek. 32:18)

- those who were trading partners with Egypt

▣ "daughters of. . ." See full notes at Jer. 46:11 and Amos 5:2.

verses.zh: 十二年十二月十五日，耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month,[NOTE:1] the Lord’s message came to me:
notes: March 17, 585 b.c. The LXX adds “first month.”
verses.commentary: 32:17 Same year as v. 1 but different month.

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要为埃及群众哀号，又要将埃及和有名之国的女子，并下坑的人，一同扔到阴府去。
verses.en: “Son of man, wail[NOTE:1] over the horde of Egypt. Bring it down;[NOTE:2] bring[NOTE:3] her[NOTE:4] and the daughters of powerful nations down to the lower parts of the earth, along with those who descend to the Pit.
notes: The Hebrew verb is used as a response to death (Jer 9:17-19; Amos 5:16).
Through this prophetic lament given by God himself, the prophet activates the judgment described therein. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:217, and L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:136-37.

Heb “Bring him down, her and the daughters of the powerful nations, to the earth below.” The verb “bring down” appears in the Hebrew text only once. Because the verb takes several objects here, the repetition of the verb in the translation improves the English style.
This apparently refers to personified Egypt.
verses.commentary:
32:18-19 These verses contain four commands, two to Ezekiel, two to Egypt.

- wail, BDB 624, KB 675, Qal IMPERATIVE, Ezek. 32:18

- bring it down, BDB 432, KB 434, Hiphil IMPERATIVE, Ezek. 32:18

- go down, BDB 432, KB 434, Qal IMPERATIVE, Ezek. 32:19

- make your bed, BDB 1011, KB 1486, Hophal IMPERATIVE, Ezek. 32:19

verses.zh: 你埃及的美丽胜过谁呢？你下去与未受割礼的人一同躺卧吧！
verses.en: Say to them,[NOTE:1] ‘Whom do you surpass in beauty?[NOTE:2] Go down and be laid to rest with the uncircumcised!’
notes: The LXX places this verse after v. 21.tn The words “say to them” are added in the translation for clarity to indicate the shift in addressee from the prophet to Egypt.
Heb “pleasantness.”

verses.zh: 他们必在被杀的人中仆到。她被交给刀剑，要把她和她的群众拉去。
verses.en: They will fall among those killed by the sword. The sword is drawn; they carry her and all her hordes away.

verses.zh: 强盛的勇士要在阴间对埃及王和帮助他的说话；他们是未受割礼被杀的人，已经下去，躺卧不动。
verses.en: The bravest of the warriors will speak to him from the midst of Sheol along with his allies, saying: ‘The uncircumcised have come down; they lie still, killed by the sword.’

verses.zh: 「亚述和她的众民都在那里，她民的坟墓在她四围；他们都是被杀倒在刀下的。
verses.en: “Assyria is there with all her assembly around her grave,[NOTE:1] all of them struck down by the sword.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “around him his graves.” The masculine pronominal suffixes are problematic; the expression is best emended to correspond to the phrase “around her grave” in v. 23. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:219.
Heb “all of them slain, the ones felled by the sword.” See as well vv. 23-24.
verses.commentary:
32:22-30 This is a series of related paragraphs/strophes that list the dead
in Sheol who greet new arrivals.

- Assyria ‒ Ezek. 32:22-23

- Elam ‒ Ezek. 32:24-25

- Anatolia ‒ Ezek. 32:26-28

- Edom ‒ Ezek. 32:29

- Syrians and Aramenians ‒ Ezek. 32:30

- Egypt ‒ Ezek. 32:31-32

In many ways this is similar to the imagery of Isaiah 14 and Ezekiel 28. The dead rejoice when
the powerful join them in Sheol and become their equals!

verses.zh: 他们的坟墓在坑中极深之处。他的众民在他坟墓的四围，都是被杀倒在刀下的；他们曾在活人之地使人惊恐。
verses.en: Their[NOTE:1] graves are located in the remote slopes of the Pit.[NOTE:2] Her assembly is around her grave, all of them struck down by the sword, those who spread terror in the land of the living.
notes: Heb “whose.”
The only other occurrence of the phrase “remote slopes of the Pit” is in Isa 14:15.
verses.commentary:
32:23 "whose graves are set in the remotest parts of the pit" This is an idiom for the worst (cf. Isa. 14:15) or lowest places in the
netherworld. They were violently slain in this world and humiliated in the next (cf. Ezek. 32:27, 32)!

Note the list of humiliated nations.

- Egypt, Ezek. 32:17-21,31

- Assyria, Ezek. 32:22-23

- Elam, Ezek. 32:24-25

- Meshech, Tubal (Anatolia), Ezek. 32:26-28

- Edom, Ezek. 32:29

- Princes of the north (i.e. Syrians or Armenians) and Sidon, Ezek. 32:30

Special Topic: Where Are the Dead?

verses.zh: 「以拦也在那里，她的群众在她坟墓的四围，都是被杀倒在刀下、未受割礼而下阴府的；他们曾在活人之地使人惊恐，并且与下坑的人一同担当羞辱。
verses.en: “Elam is there with all her hordes around her grave; all of them struck down by the sword. They went down uncircumcised to the lower parts of the earth, those who spread terror in the land of the living. Now they will bear their shame with those who descend to the Pit.

verses.zh: 人给她和她的群众在被杀的人中设立床榻。她民的坟墓在她四围，他们都是未受割礼被刀杀的；他们曾在活人之地使人惊恐，并且与下坑的人一同担当羞辱。以拦已经放在被杀的人中。
verses.en: Among the dead they have made a bed for her, along with all her hordes around her grave.[NOTE:1] All of them are uncircumcised, killed by the sword, for their terror had spread in the land of the living. They bear their shame along with those who descend to the Pit; they are placed among the dead.
notes: Heb “around him her graves,” but the expression is best emended to read “around her grave” (see vv. 23-24).

verses.zh: 「米设、土巴，和她们的群众都在那里。她民的坟墓在她四围，他们都是未受割礼被刀杀的；他们曾在活人之地使人惊恐。
verses.en: “Meshech Tubal is there, along with all her hordes around her grave.[NOTE:1] All of them are uncircumcised, killed by the sword, for they spread their terror in the land of the living.
notes: Heb “around him her graves,” but the expression is best emended to read “around her grave” (see vv. 23-24).
verses.commentary:
32:26 "Meshech, Tubal" These two nations/regions were located north of Israel/Judah (cf. Ezek. 39:2).

- Meshech (BDB 604, KB 646 II)

- north of the Black Sea

- central Anatolia

- see full note at Ezek. 38:2

- Tubal (BDB 1063, KB 1683) was a nation/region

- in eastern Anatolia (Asia Minor)

- in Cappadocia (Josephus)

- see fuller note at Ezek. 38:2

verses.zh: 他们不得与那未受割礼仆倒的勇士一同躺卧；这些勇士带着兵器下阴间，头枕刀剑，骨头上有本身的罪孽；他们曾在活人之地使勇士惊恐。
verses.en: They do not lie with the fallen warriors of ancient times,[NOTE:1] who went down to Sheol with their weapons of war, having their swords placed under their heads and their shields on their bones,[NOTE:2] when the terror of these warriors was in the land of the living.
notes: Heb “of the uncircumcised.” The LXX reads, probably correctly, “from of old” rather than “of the uncircumcised.” The phrases are very similar in spelling. The warriors of Meshech Tubal are described as uncircumcised, so it would be odd for them to not be buried with the uncircumcised. Verse 28 specifically says that they would lie with the uncircumcised.

Heb “and their iniquities were over their bones.” The meaning of this statement is unclear. In light of the parallelism (see “swords”) it is preferable to emend עֲוֹנֹתָם (ʿavonotam; “their iniquities”) to צִנּוֹתָם or צִנָּתָם (tsinnotam or tsinnatam; “their shields” or “their shield”) See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:135.
verses.commentary:
32:27

NASB, NKJV, Peshitta, REB, JPSOA
"uncircumcised"

LXX, NRSV, TEV, NJB
"long ago"

The phrases are spelled similarly in Hebrew

- MT, "from among the uncircumcised" מערלים

- LXX, "of old" םעולם

The second fits the context best (NET, p. 1514) because these people were part of the uncircumcised and the term is
repeated in Ezek. 32:28. The UBS Text Project, p. 112, gives the LXX version a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

NASB, NKJV, JPSOA, LXX, Peshitta
"their iniquity rested on

their bones"

NRSV, TEV
"whose shields are upon

their bones"

NJB
"their shields put under

their bones"

REB
"their shields over their

bones"

These men of Meshech, Tubal are honored even in death, but not so for the Egyptians!

The UBS Text Project, p. 113, gives "their iniquity" (BDB 730, KB 800) an "A" rating. However, many translations
emend it to "shields" (BDB 857 III, KB 1037 II)

- better parallel to "weapons of war" and "swords" under their heads

- similar spelling of "iniquity"

- "their iniquity" עונתם

- "their shields" צנותם

verses.zh: 「法老啊，你必在未受割礼的人中败坏，与那些被杀的人一同躺卧。
verses.en: “But as for you, in the midst of the uncircumcised you will be broken, and you will lie with those killed by the sword.

verses.zh: 「以东也在那里。她君王和一切首领虽然仗着势力，还是放在被杀的人中；他们必与未受割礼的和下坑的人一同躺卧。
verses.en: “Edom is there with her kings and all her princes. Despite their might they are laid with those killed by the sword; they lie with the uncircumcised and those who descend to the Pit.

verses.zh: 「在那里有北方的众王子和一切西顿人，都与被杀的人下去。他们虽然仗着势力使人惊恐，还是蒙羞。他们未受割礼，和被刀杀的一同躺卧，与下坑的人一同担当羞辱。
verses.en: “All the leaders of the north are there, along with all the Sidonians; despite their might they have gone down in shameful terror with the dead. They lie uncircumcised with those killed by the sword and bear their shame with those who descend to the Pit.

verses.zh: 「法老看见他们，便为他被杀的军队受安慰。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: “Pharaoh will see them and be consoled over all his hordes who were killed by the sword, Pharaoh and all his army, declares the Sovereign Lord.

verses.zh: 我任凭法老在活人之地使人惊恐，法老和他的群众必放在未受割礼和被杀的人中。这是主耶和华说的。」
verses.en: Indeed, I terrified him in the land of the living, yet he will lie in the midst of the uncircumcised with those killed by the sword, Pharaoh and all his hordes, declares the Sovereign Lord.”

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the four modern translations above.
Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.
